title: Book Bus Tickets Early for Diwali and Chhath 2026
summary: Diwali falls on 8 November 2026 and Chhath on 15 November. Know why festive fares climb and when to book bus tickets early for both peaks.
body_markdown:
November 2026 carries two separate travel peaks, not one long festive stretch. Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November, and the main Chhath arghya on Sunday, 15 November. Travellers who plan them as a single block usually discover the problem on the return leg, when the cheaper fare options on their corridor have already gone.


# How November 2026 Splits Into Two Travel Peaks


The first wave builds from Dhanteras on 6 November and eases after Bhai Dooj on 10 November. The second begins around 12 November, when families move towards Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh for the four days of Chhath, which close on 16 November.


This guide sets out the confirmed dates for both windows, explains what actually lifts intercity fares in those weeks, and suggests a booking timeline. Live fares and seat counts for any corridor sit on the[zingbus route and city booking pages](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets) for your travel date.


## Why It Helps to Book Bus Tickets Early Diwali Chhath Season


Festive demand on private intercity buses does not spread evenly across the month. It concentrates on roughly six departure nights, and on those nights the constraint is availability as much as fare. Travellers who book bus tickets early during the Diwali Chhath season are mostly buying choice: the departure time they want, the boarding point closest to home, and a berth rather than whatever is left.


## Two Peaks, Not One Festive Block


Keeping the two events separate makes the booking decision far simpler. Each has its own outbound night, its own quiet day and its own return crunch.


**Occasion** **Date in 2026** **Where the travel pressure sits**


Dhanteras Friday, 6 November Outbound demand starts building on the Thursday and Friday


Choti Diwali Saturday, 7 November The single busiest outbound night for the Diwali window


Diwali Sunday, 8 November Intercity travel thins out as people are already home


Govardhan Puja Monday, 9 November State holiday in several states, so return travel stays light


Bhai Dooj Tuesday, 10 November Short sibling visits, then the first big return wave


Nahay Khay Friday, 13 November Second outbound wave towards Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh


Sandhya Arghya Sunday, 15 November Travel near the ghat cities is local rather than intercity


Usha Arghya Monday, 16 November Return demand starts that evening and peaks on 17 November


Dev Deepawali Tuesday, 24 November A separate Varanasi bound spike, unrelated to the Chhath rush


**Note:** Chhath dates follow the tithi rather than the clock, so the calendar date can shift by a day in some regions. Confirm against a current panchang for your city before you lock a non refundable plan around the arghya timings.


## What Actually Pushes Festive Bus Fares Up


Private intercity fares are not fixed the way a railway chart is. They move with how much of a specific bus on a specific date has already sold, which is why the same route can look cheap in September and expensive in the first week of November.


Three things stack up in festive weeks:


- Demand collapses onto a handful of nights. A corridor that normally spreads its load across seven days is trying to move the same passengers on two or three departures.
- Traffic runs one way. Buses leave Delhi NCR full towards Lucknow, Gorakhpur and Patna, and come back with empty seats, so the outbound leg carries the cost of the round trip.
- The cheapest inventory sells first. Late buyers are not paying a penalty, they are simply seeing the fares that remain after the lower buckets have gone.


None of this makes early booking a guaranteed saving on every route. It does mean the range of options is widest early and narrowest in the final week, and on peak nights the narrowing is severe.


**Note:** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## The Return Date Is the Harder Booking


Most people book the outbound leg the moment leave is approved and leave the return open. In festive weeks that is backwards. Outbound demand spreads across two or three nights, while returns cluster hard on one or two.


For the Diwali window, expect the squeeze on 10 and 11 November. For Chhath, it lands on the evening of 16 November and through 17 November, once the morning arghya is done and working families head back. Booking both legs in the same sitting removes the part of the trip that usually goes wrong.


## A Booking Timeline That Fits the 2026 Calendar


These are practical markers rather than deadlines. Adjust them if your corridor is a small one with only one or two daily departures, because those sell out well ahead of the bigger routes.


- Diwali outbound, travelling 6 or 7 November: settle it through the second half of October.
- Diwali return, travelling 10 or 11 November: book it in the same session as the outbound leg.
- Chhath outbound, travelling 12 or 13 November: aim for the last week of October, earlier on thin routes.
- Chhath return, travelling 16 or 17 November: this is the tightest leg of the month, so treat it as the priority.
- Dev Deepawali in Varanasi on 24 November: a long weekend runs from Saturday 21 November, with 24 November also being a gazetted holiday for Guru Nanak Jayanti, so the city fills earlier than people expect.


## Departure Times That Hold Up in Festive Traffic


An overnight departure is usually the sensible festive choice, though the reason is arrival time rather than comfort. A bus leaving Delhi NCR in the evening reaches most Uttar Pradesh cities in the early morning, which leaves the whole day for onward travel to a town or village.


Two practical points apply in these specific weeks. Highway exits from major cities crawl on the evenings before a festival, so a late evening departure can lose an hour before it reaches the open road. And if you are travelling for Chhath itself, plan to arrive a full day before the Sandhya Arghya rather than on the morning of it, since the offering is tied to sunset and does not wait for a delayed bus.


## Boarding Points and Baggage Need More Thought Than Usual


Pick a boarding point you can reach without depending on peak city traffic. A terminal counter is easier to find in the dark and in a crowd than a roadside pickup, particularly if you are travelling with parents or small children. Reaching the boarding point 20 to 30 minutes early matters more in festive weeks, when a single delayed passenger holds up a full bus.


Baggage is the other festive difference. Sweets, gift boxes and extra clothing push most families past their normal load, and zingbus applies a limit of 15 kg per passenger on its services. Packing fragile items in hand baggage rather than the hold is worth the effort on a nine hour journey.


## If Your Leave Dates Are Still Uncertain


Uncertain dates are the real reason people delay booking, and the delay costs more than the flexibility is worth. Read the[current cancellation and refund policy](https://www.zingbus.com/policies) before booking so you know what a date change actually costs on your fare type.


For anyone who travels the same corridor several times a year, zingprime adds cancellation flexibility that is worth checking against your own travel pattern. It is a membership decision rather than a festive one, so evaluate it on how often you travel, not on a single Diwali trip.


## Getting Your November Seats Settled


The festive calendar this year is unusually easy to plan around. Diwali on a Sunday and the Chhath arghya on the following Sunday create two clean windows with a working week between them, and the return dates that will hurt are already visible on the calendar.


Fix the two return legs first, then the outbound ones, then the boarding point. If you are travelling towards Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Patna or Varanasi, check live options on your corridor now rather than in the first week of November, when the only decision left will be whichever departure still has seats.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### When is Diwali in 2026?


Diwali in 2026 falls on Sunday, 8 November, with Dhanteras on 6 November, Choti Diwali on 7 November and Bhai Dooj on 10 November.


### When is Chhath Puja in 2026?


Chhath Puja in 2026 runs from 13 to 16 November, with the Sandhya Arghya on Sunday, 15 November and the Usha Arghya on Monday, 16 November.


### How early should I book bus tickets for early Diwali Chhath travel?


Book bus tickets early Diwali Chhath travel through the second half of October, and treat thin routes with one or two daily departures as even more urgent.


### Why do bus fares rise before Diwali?


Bus fares rise before Diwali because demand concentrates on a few nights, buses return with empty seats, and the lowest fare inventory sells out first.


### Which travel dates are the busiest in the Diwali window?


The busiest dates in the Diwali window are the outbound nights of 6 and 7 November and the return legs on 10 and 11 November.


### Which dates are busiest around Chhath?


Around Chhath the busiest dates are 12 and 13 November for outbound travel, and the evening of 16 November through 17 November for returns.


### Is it cheaper to book a bus one way or both ways together?


Booking both ways together is not automatically cheaper, but it protects the return leg, which is the scarcer seat in every festive week.


### Do fares ever fall closer to the festival date?


Fares occasionally soften on a low demand departure, but waiting for that on a peak festive night usually means paying more for fewer options.


### Should I take a day bus or an overnight bus during the festive season?


An overnight bus suits festive travel better because it reaches most destinations by morning and leaves the full day free for onward local travel.


### How much luggage can I carry on a zingbus service?


zingbus applies a limit of 15 kg per passenger, so pack gift boxes and sweets carefully and keep fragile items with you rather than below.


### Is Dev Deepawali part of the same festive rush?


Dev Deepawali is a separate spike on 24 November 2026, focused on Varanasi, and it needs its own booking rather than the Chhath plan.


### What if my leave dates change after booking?


Check the current cancellation policy before booking, because rebooking during a festive week usually means accepting whatever departure and fare remain.


### How far in advance do small town routes sell out?


Small town routes with only one or two daily departures can sell out several weeks ahead, so they deserve earlier attention than major city corridors.
